Today a joint compromise petition is filed under Section 320 of CrPC.
2.
Respondent No.2/defacto complainant is present before this Court.

On being specifically queried,
NC: 2025:KHC:34861 HC-KAR she acknowledges the settlement recorded in M.C. No.2961/2020.

She further affirms that the marriage between herself and petitioner No.1 has since been dissolved and, in terms of the compromise, a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- was paid to her during the course of the matrimonial proceedings in M.C. No.2961/2020.

In view of the said amicable settlement,
respondent No.2 has voluntarily withdrawn all allegations made in the complaint and has no objection for quashing of the criminal proceedings pending in C.C. No.7077/2020.

sentences.text: It is also placed on record that petitioner No.1 was required to pay the balance settlement amount of Rs.1,00,000/- to respondent No.2.
The said amount has been duly transferred in open Court today through Google Pay to respondent No.2, who has acknowledged receipt of the same.

4. Having regard to the above facts and circumstances, this Court is satisfied that the dispute NC:
2025:KHC:34861 HC-KAR between the parties, which essentially arose out of matrimonial discord,
has been amicably settled once and for all.

Though the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC is not compoundable under Section 320 Cr.P.C., the Hon'ble Apex Court has time and again recognized that in cases arising out of matrimonial disputes, the High Court, in exercise of its inherent powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., can quash the proceedings to secure the ends of justice and to give a quietus to the dispute.
5.
Accordingly, taking note of the settlement and the statement made by respondent No.2/complainant, this petition deserves to be allowed.

6. Hence, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The petition is hereby allowed.

(ii) The proceedings in C.C. No.7077/2020 pending on the file of the 49th Additional Chief NC: 2025:KHC:34861 HC-KAR Metropolitan Magistrate, Nrupathunga Road,
Bengaluru City, are hereby quashed.
